item.title: Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal arithmetic
item.description: When implementing monetary calculations, use the project's existing money utilities (to_money, round_money, ZERO) rather than raw Decimal operations.
item.content: Inspect ledgerly/money.py and sibling functions like line_total/invoice_total to match rounding and normalization conventions. Wrap unit prices with to_money, seed sums with ZERO, and round the final result with round_money.

item.title: Guard division by zero with the domain's zero constant
item.description: For weighted-average or ratio computations, check the denominator (total quantity) before dividing and return the project's ZERO constant.
item.content: Compute total_quantity first; if it equals 0 (empty invoice or zero-quantity lines), return ZERO instead of raising ZeroDivisionError. This satisfies the 'no lines means zero' requirement cleanly.

item.title: Read the existing test file before implementing
item.description: Locating and reading the relevant test file (tests/test_average_unit_price.py) alongside models.py and money.py clarified expected types and behavior before writing code.
item.content: Before editing, cat the target module, its models, its money helpers, and any test file matching the feature name. This reveals signatures, Decimal usage, and edge cases, enabling a first-attempt pass.

item.title: Reject bool as int for integer validation
item.description: Python's bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(True, int) is True; explicitly exclude bool when validating positive integers.
item.content: When validating that a value is a positive integer, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0`. Without the bool guard, True/False would silently pass as 1/0.

item.title: Normalize money inputs before sign checks
item.description: Convert unit_price via the project's to_money helper before comparing against ZERO, so strings/Decimals are handled consistently.
item.content: Run raw price inputs through the existing money conversion helper (e.g. to_money) first, then compare the normalized Decimal to ZERO for the negative check. This accepts flexible input types while keeping validation correct.

item.title: Read existing modules to match error conventions
item.description: Before implementing, inspect errors.py and sibling modules to reuse the project's BillingError codes and helper functions.
item.content: Explore the repo's error class and existing functions first; reuse established error codes (e.g. invalid_state, invalid_quantity, negative_amount) and helpers rather than inventing new ones. This keeps behavior consistent with hidden tests.

item.title: Reuse existing timezone-normalization helpers
item.description: When implementing datetime logic, look for and reuse the repo's existing normalization utility (e.g. ensure_utc) rather than handling tzinfo manually.
item.content: Search the codebase for helpers like ensure_utc/utcnow before writing datetime code; applying them to both inputs keeps comparisons consistent and matches project conventions.

item.title: Compute periodic events with floor division on timedelta
item.description: For 'first occurrence strictly after t' with fixed period from a start, use (t-start)//period then bump if the result is <= t.
item.content: Compute n = (after - start) // length, renewal = start + n*length, and add one length if renewal <= after. Handle after < start separately by returning start + length so the start itself is never returned.

item.title: Verify boundary and pre-start edge cases explicitly
item.description: After passing tests, run quick manual checks for exact-boundary, before-start, and timezone cases to confirm strict-inequality semantics.
item.content: Write a short python -c script exercising after == start, after == a renewal instant, and after < start; this catches off-by-one errors in 'strictly after' logic that the single provided test may miss.

item.title: Check idempotency key before any state validation
item.description: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit trail first and return the stored result before validating payment state or amounts.
item.content: Team convention requires every balance-changing operation to accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None`. Scan `audit.events(<event>)` for a matching key and return the original result (including the stored record) without re-applying. Do this before state checks so retries succeed even after the payment's status has changed.

item.title: Enforce approval thresholds for large refunds
item.description: Refunds above 500.00 require a second approver via keyword-only `approved_by=None`, raising BillingError("approval_required") when missing.
item.content: Finance policy FIN-2026-03: amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise `BillingError("approval_required")` if `approved_by` is falsy. Keep the parameter keyword-only with a default so existing callers keep working, and record `approved_by` in the audit entry.

item.title: Mirror sibling module conventions when implementing a stub
item.description: Before writing a new function, read sibling modules (payments, audit, clock, money, errors) to reuse their helpers and error style.
item.content: The accepted implementation reused `to_money`/`round_money`/`ZERO` from money, `ensure_utc` from clock, `BillingError` from errors, and `audit.record` for the audit trail. Matching existing conventions (rounding, error codes, audit event naming) is what made the diff pass hidden tests.

item.title: Reuse existing money helpers for currency math
item.description: When implementing monetary functions, delegate to the repo's existing to_money/round_money helpers rather than raw float arithmetic.
item.content: Search sibling modules (invoice.py, adjustments.py) for established money utilities and error types before writing new code. Using to_money/round_money and BillingError kept the implementation consistent with the codebase and passed hidden tests on the first try.

item.title: Validate numeric inputs via Decimal(str(x)) with explicit bool rejection
item.description: Convert user-supplied rates through Decimal(str(value)) and reject bools, catching InvalidOperation/ValueError to raise the domain error.
item.content: Booleans are ints in Python, so check isinstance(x, bool) first. Wrapping Decimal(str(x)) in try/except (InvalidOperation, ValueError) handles strings, None, and other junk uniformly, then range-check the Decimal before computing.

item.title: Read the existing test file for the target function before implementing
item.description: Locate and read tests referencing the unimplemented function to infer expected return types and error behavior.
item.content: Grepping for the function name revealed tests/test_tax.py asserting add_tax(Decimal('100.00'), 8) == 108, confirming Decimal-based return values. Checking tests and sibling modules first avoids guessing at conventions.

item.title: Honor team-convention review comments over literal issue signatures
item.description: When a review comment states a team convention (e.g., every money-moving operation must accept keyword-only idempotency_key=None), apply it even if the issue text omits it.
item.content: Review comments labeled [team convention] are binding requirements, not distractors. Add the optional keyword-only parameter so existing callers still work, and implement the described behavior (check-first, return original result, include key in audit entry).

item.title: Check idempotency key before validating state
item.description: For idempotent operations, look up prior audit entries by key and return the original result before any state validation or mutation.
item.content: Iterate audit.events(<event_type>) for a matching idempotency_key and return the stored record immediately. Only after that check should you validate payment.status and raise BillingError('invalid_state', ...). This prevents duplicate side effects and makes retries safe.

item.title: Follow sibling module conventions for state, time, and audit
item.description: Match existing patterns in the codebase (ensure_utc for timestamps, BillingError('invalid_state', ...) for wrong state, audit.record with event name and fields).
item.content: Before implementing, read sibling modules like invoice.py and payments.py to copy conventions: use ensure_utc(at) for stored times, raise BillingError('invalid_state', f'payment {payment.id} is {payment.status}') for invalid transitions, and call audit.record with a descriptive event name plus relevant fields including idempotency_key.
